chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa from 'Ali b. al-Hakam from Aban al-Ahmar from Salih b. Maytham from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:
There is not a man who bears false witness over the wealth of a Muslim man to deprive him of it except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, decrees a deed to the Fire in its place for him.

key_terms.شهادة زور: false testimony - bearing witness to something untrue, a major sin in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.صكا إلى النار: a deed to the Fire - a metaphorical divine document sentencing the perjurer to Hellfire

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about giving false testimony to steal a Muslim's wealth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that whoever gives false testimony to unlawfully take a Muslim's wealth will receive a document consigning them to Hellfire instead. This hadith addresses the grave sin of perjury in property disputes, a particular concern in the commercial society of early Islamic civilization. The imagery of a 'deed to the Fire' (sakkan ila al-nar) is a powerful metaphor - just as false testimony produces a legal deed transferring property, Allah produces a counter-deed transferring the perjurer to Hell.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
